text_fidelity_a:
Hog Wild Toys Air Strike Catapult We discovered these recently at a local library fair. The theme was time travel through history and these were used in the medieval area in a game of breaching the castle wall and trying to knock its occupants from their perch! Each of my five children ages 3-12 (not to mention my husband!) Were so enamored with these that I ended up ordering some on my phone before we even left the building.

We received them in the mail today and have yet to stop playing with them. To make the most of their playability, I ordered two catapults and one set of extra balls (6 in a pkg). I highly recommend the extra balls as we have already lost two inside our house. They seem to be of sturdy construction and are very fairly priced, but as to longevity of use or under harsher hands, I cannot yet determine.

Overall, I recommend this if you are looking for a fun toy, great for all ages, with some educational value (learning about arch and propulsion). Enjoy the impending assault!

Mattel Disney Sofia The First Vacation Palace Playset Apparently this Auntie is the bomb for getting a certain 6 year old niece this Sofia the First Vacation Playset. My niece is an avid Sofia the First fan so anything that remotely smacks of Sofia is a must have. The castle isn't a whole unit, the back side is open so little hands can really get into the play. It lifts up to drop down the "water" play area complete with a merry-go-round in the form of a ship's wheel. This playset only comes with Sofia (who is stuck as a mermaid except when you clip her dress on). Of course, this means I'll have pieces to purchase to make it full set, but I'm okay with that. The playset isn't too terribly sturdy but it isn't cheaply made either. It's exactly what I've come to expect from all playsets lately - not made to last forever. Price-wise, you are paying for the Disney name. If I was to guess the value, I'd say right around $15 which is much less than the current $28 price tag. That being said, the joy that it brought my niece was well worth it. The price makes me go with four stars. If I was going simply off my niece's enthusiasm, it would easily earn 5 stars.

PLEASE NOTE: To purchase this castle, the family set ($22.99) and the animals (prices vary) will put you well over $60. Something to consider when making the purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Disney Sofia The First Vacation Palace Playset

text_fidelity_a:
Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In We've been playing with Vector for a little over a month now, and he's a load of fun! At first, he didn't do a lot, but every so often, Anki provides an update and suddenly, Vector has more personality, skills, and interactions! He's a great little desk companion that is much better than a pet because there's little to clean up afterward! I say little because he's been known to shove things off the table!
There are many ways he can learn about his environment via his sensors:
He sees via HD camera.
Facial recognition - he'll learn your face and when he's exploring, will come right up, scan your face, and say your name! He's very pleased when he recognizes you, and gets a little upset if he doesn't recognize you.
Navigate, explore, and learn his environment. He gets around very well all over my desk. However, I move things a lot, so he's constantly having to re-learn. Occasionally, he'll fall over the edge, but once in a while, he falls over the edge. I think they're working on improving that a lot. It's super cute when he's exploring, gets close to the edge, and acts scared and backs away!
If he needs charging, he'll go right back to his charger on his own. However, sometimes, I'll get tired of hearing him causing trouble, so I'll tell him to go to his charger. He does it, but throws a little tantrum when he gets there!

He can hear via his array of four microphones. Sometimes he comes over to see what's going on if you're having a conversation. If he's resting, he'll act startled if there's a loud noise in the room. He will also react to the beat of music if it's loud and near him. If you ask him to look at you or come here, he'll be able to sense the direction to go.

He reacts to touch and feel. If you pet his back, he practically purrs! But shaking him gets a reaction, too!

He has amazing intelligence. For instance, he answers questions, plays blackjack, reacts to his environment, and senses actions and activities around him.

He speaks to you. I'm not a fan of his synthesized voice, but it seems to be improving. When he reads out answers to questions you ask, sometimes it's hard to hear what he's saying. However, as they receive feedback on this, I'm sure his voice will evolve into something more understandable.

We really enjoy seeing his reactions! The current one is the way he gets super excited when you tell him he's a good robot or if you tell him you love him, and pouts a little if you tell him he's a bad robot! I just told him earlier today when he picked up his cube and tossed it off the desk!

I'm super excited to see his ever-evolving skills! I highly recommend this little guy for your favorite tech lover, or yourself! If you're looking for a toy for younger kids, maybe go with a Cosmo. This doesn't have games or things to entertain little ones. But it's completely entertaining for maybe, 10 years and up robotics fans!
text_fidelity_b: Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In

text_fidelity_a:
AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5 This was delivered to my house about an hour ago, and my 6 year old daughter is about to put it away. She's just now finishing up the hardest puzzle included in the kit.

I'm torn on how to review this. It's clearly a nice toy for a lot of kids. The pieces are nice and chunky, the puzzle cards have vibrant artwork, and the app works smoothly. That said, though, there are 12 puzzle cards in the box, and yes, they can be solved multiple ways, but there is no guidance for different combinations of blocks to use to complete the puzzles, so there isn't much incentive to take them off and try again. Also, for someone who is not too far removed from the minimum age range suggested though, it's really easy. Like, a puzzle in two minutes for almost every combo in the deck, except for the boat, which is in the middle of the difficulty spectrum. On the box, with an oddly small top, there are images of three-dimensional shapes made out of the aniblocks, flying around, and the actual blocks do not connect in this way to form them, which was probably the most disappointing part.

The app deserves some special mention. It's certainly good, and easy to use, but it's still an app, and so, of course, it defeats the purpose of having a screen avoidant time to include it. There's also another disadvantage, which is that there are tons of apps that do this same game already, with digital blocks. They offer more puzzles, with more diverse colors of blocks, in more diverse shapes, and a wider variety of difficulty levels.

Overall, I think there are better toys for your money that do very similar things and offer a lot more variety than this. The phone apps, as mentioned before. We have a board game called Blokus 3D (or Rumis) which have a similar pattern-matching idea, but allow for 3D building. There's also Kanoodle Junior, for example, which is excellent, cheaper, ready to travel, and doesn't require an app. 12 puzzles and a handful of two-colored blocks is just not enough for the price. For that reason, I cannot recommend this...but there are far worse options.
text_fidelity_b: AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5

The second item to not fair well (or maybe contents settled in transit) was one of the battery packs, as I was putting batteries in the unit the coil sprung out and while I can gently set it back in there it doesn't stay attached when one removes the battery. The connectors for some of the circuits also don't stay snapped together very well, it is like some of them have a little bigger opening than others. I have heard such great reviews about these products and some of the labs are genuinely cool (like the fiber optic labs) but at this point I'm not sure what to do as it is probably only 50% usable of what I thought we were getting due to the build quality. Again great ideas and I'm sure others have had better luck than me and I understand that all products are not 100% perfect all of the time but this was a Christmas gift and I'm feeling a little bit like we wasted some money here on this one.

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Winning Moves No Stress Chess, Natural (1091) for 2 players My daughter (8 years) really took an interest in a chess a few years ago. We played regular chess, but it wasn't that engaging. This levels the playing field and is really fun, even if you understand play chess a lot. The game focuses on drawing cards that tell you want piece to move. Based on the card, it poses different scenarios that either level the playing field or draws the game a bit longer. For example, being in check and not drawing a king card to move out or not drawing a card to neutralize the check. My daughter had made some gear combos with the pieces in her hand. There are really three modes

(1) each player draws one card and that is the card to move. (Easiest)
(2) each player has 3 cards and plays a piece from that
(3) each player has 5 cards and plays a piece from one of those cards

I'm surprised this hasn't been invented before. It is great if you've never played chess or have played chess and want to teach someone new.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Winning Moves No Stress Chess, Natural (1091) for 2 players

ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner We received this toy tonight and my youngest daughter (5 years old) used all the paint making some really cool spin art for me. Overall, I think it is a wonderful activity for children that was surprisingly NOT messy. Of course, the "splash guard" that is included looks A LOT like trash (luckily they have a small sticker that tells you it is the splash guard and not to be thrown away).

It takes one "C" battery which we had on hand (luckily) and we were good to go. My daughter had a blast and once I showed her where to place the corners she had no problem doing it all on her own. The paper is like (black and white)card stock and even though it curls a bit at first after getting painted but eventually it lays down flat. We used both colors but only the white color works nicely. The black doesn't show the colors good and after the paint dries you can't hardly see it so do yourself a favor and use the white side. The only other problem I see is that the glitter tubes should have a shaker end since younger kids have real problems shaking anything out of an open tube.

I have a feeling we will be going get more paint (and paper) really soon because it was a hit with my daughters and we taped their art work to the computer cabinet.

text_fidelity_a:
Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women I could not tell exactly how these “puzzles” work, even after looking at the video. You have to do two different things. First you have to “flip” each of the circles back-and-forth until you get all of them flipped to the correct side. Then you have to “spin” each of the circles to align them correctly. I find that it’s best to start from the outside circle and work your way in. The “puzzles” with most similar colors / designs on each side are the most challenging to work to get the circles on the correct side.

FYI. . . Once you have completed one side, the opposite side will not be complete. So though you will not have to flip the circles. . You’ll have to rotate the circles to complete the puzzle. So you’ll always have one side complete, and one size incomplete.

It should be noted that this “puzzle” is sturdy enough for a puzzle such as this, but it can certainly be pulled apart and broken without too much effort.

I think this “puzzle” to be best for ages tweens and up. It’s not super challenging, but again the ones with the common colors on both sides are the most challenging.

This puzzle is Made in China and being sold by a Canadian company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women

text_fidelity_a:
Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi This is a very simple stock market game that is somewhat accessible to younger players. Throughout the game, you'll buy and sell ingredients, complete potions with special abilities, and manipulate a cool little stock market simulation gadget that rolls colored containers down a ramp to indicate value.

The game is very simple, and offers players, in my opinion, a few too many options during their turn. Adults and gamers will find that the ability to sell sets at maximum value to be pretty easy because of the ability to sell not only sets, but individual cards (which allows you to essentially set any price for any set you like). To obtain new ingredients, you can buy from the market, buy from the deck, or swap, or use potion effects. That's a lot of choices to handle, and our little gamer found it to be confusing at first because there were simply too many options. She could identify which cards she wanted, but didn't know whether she should buy, trade or use effects to get them.

All told, this is a good game for youngsters, but there is a learning curve to get good. The number of options can be overwhelming and frustrating at first, but after a few plays, anyone as young as six or eight can probably grasp how to do some of the more complex manipulations. I don't think this will ever be a go-to for an adult game night, but for families, you could do a lot worse than this.

Also, the components are great.
text_fidelity_b: Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi

text_fidelity_a:
Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot This is video pinball as it used to be, before today's highly sophisticated physics simulators: floaty ball mechanics, dumbed down special features, bizarre flipper behavior, etc. Which is what I expected.

But I have to say, I'm impressed at the care they put into it nevertheless. They carefully reproduced the major playfield features and loops, the special modes, the multiballs, the spinning pizza. They made the marquee its whole own separate screen so they could have the interactive elements. They have a clever alternative for the plunger (hold down the button for longer to shoot harder). The flipper buttons on the side can get a little finger-cramping, so they put duplicates on the back of the unit so you can hold the whole unit. And, for better or for worse, they reproduced all of the boys' voices. Ugh. And unless I'm mistaken, unlike most of the Tiny Arcade series, it actually saves your high scores.

It's not all good - the "Start Game"/"Game Over" text is hilariously blocky, like an Atari 2600 game, and it pops up on the playfield. I don't know why they didn't put it on the marquee LCD where it belonged. The ball vibrates weirdly on the habitrails. A couple times, particularly in multiball, I've had the ball just simply fall through the hinge of the flipper. But these aren't huge concerns, and they're easily laughed off.

One warning for sensitive and/or young users: I've always thought the original pinball game's marquee's presentation of April was excessively sexy (she's a hero in her own right, not eye candy, darn it) but in the cut down version it looks like... uh, something else entirely.

All in all, this way exceeded my expectations. And it's actually quite fun! I'm not interested in the other "boardwalk arcade" games so far, but I'd gladly buy more pinball games like this one if they're at a similar level of playability.
text_fidelity_b: Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot

The parts of this kit snap together on a clear plastic grid. The instruction book is a black and white center stapled pamphlet that can be challenging to decipher for builds that are more complex. The kit seems durable but not indestructable. My kids can be pretty rough on things so they have been using this kit with my supervision.

For most kids under 10, this is not the type of toy that they can play with on their own. I have my son use this toy at the dining room table. We check to make sure that all of the parts get back in their place when we are done.

This is an educational toy. My experience is that early exposure to learning experiences like this can shape interests later on in life.

I would have liked to have seen a description of what the various modules do to the electricity to make the magic happen.

Though it’s colorful, and there is the aspect of flipping the car. . . . as you can see from the video. . . it only takes a second or two for the car to go around, and then you’re done.  There is simply not enough “excitement” to keep a child engaged for very long.
